comparison: Both evaluate the transcriptome-wide analysis of LAST targets (C76-C82). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with convergence of RNA-seq and RIP-seq data. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether overlap is statistically significant and whether validation is comprehensive enough.

Both address LAST's specific effect on CCND1 and cell cycle (C23-C29, C103). OpenEval finds the specificity controls and flow cytometry data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED as part of the overall convincing experimental work.

Both evaluate c-Myc regulation of LAST (C11, C17-C22). OpenEval finds the multiple experimental approaches (ChIP, luciferase, etc.) provide SUPPORTED converging evidence. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED without challenge as part of high-quality work.

Both address CNBP-CCND1 binding site mapping (C58-C64, C68-C75). OpenEval finds deletion mapping and RIP-seq provide SUPPORTED evidence for precise localization. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about RIP-seq methodology, questioning how binding sites were determined without digestion.

OpenEval R6 evaluates molecular characterization through EMSA and mutagenesis (C65-C75), finding it SUPPORTED. This overlaps with peer R5's UNCERTAINTY about the RIP-seq methodology used to identify these binding motifs.

Both address post-transcriptional regulation mechanism. OpenEval R4 covers CNBP's mediator role (C39-C57) as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates the post-transcriptional mechanism (C31-C32, C34-C35, C46-C56) as SUPPORTED, with reviewers finding the case 'quite convincing.'

OpenEval R4 addresses CNBP's mediator role (C39-C57). Peer R1 evaluates the overall mechanistic claims including some CNBP-related claims (C39, C42-C45, C52, C57) as SUPPORTED, stating authors made a 'quite convincing case.'

Both address transcriptional vs post-transcriptional regulation. OpenEval R3 finds the distinction (C31-C38) SUPPORTED through actinomycin D chase and RNA pull-down. Peer R10 also finds the post-transcriptional mechanism (C31-C32, C34-C35) SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R3 evaluates mechanistic distinction between transcriptional/post-transcriptional regulation (C31-C38). Peer R1 includes some overlapping claims (C33, C36-C38) in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation of the core mechanism.

Both address xenograft tumor formation data (C83-C84, C88). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as part of oncogenic role demonstration. Peer reviewers also find xenograft data SUPPORTED without specific critique.

Both evaluate TCGA clinical correlation analysis (C85-C87). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED despite negative correlation results. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting the lack of anti-correlation between CCND1 and LAST is 'important negative data' that questions biological significance.

Both address negative TCGA findings (C106-C107). OpenEval finds these appropriately reported as SUPPORTED, indicating regulatory complexity. Peer reviewers view this as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing it as important negative data that should be discussed regarding biological significance.

Both address cis vs trans regulation (C119-C120). OpenEval finds the evidence for trans regulation SUPPORTED but notes the co-localization conclusion is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers find it SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the rescue experiment demonstrates trans action.

OpenEval R2 includes C30 (adjacent gene control) as part of LAST's specificity evidence, finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R3 specifically requested this control experiment and accepted the data as SUPPORTED in revision.

OpenEval R1 includes FISH localization data (C15) as SUPPORTED evidence for LAST characterization. Peer R4 expresses UNCERTAINTY about FISH probe specificity due to transposable element composition, requesting additional validation.
OpenEval R14 evaluates high-level summary claims (C1, C3-C6) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes some of these claims (C1, C3) in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation of the core mechanistic findings.
OpenEval R14 includes summary claims about oncogenic function (C5-C6). Peer R7 evaluates related xenograft data (C5-C6, C83-C84, C88, C104) as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R14 includes C4 (summary of additional targets). Peer R6 evaluates the detailed transcriptome-wide analysis (C4, C76-C82) with UNCERTAINTY about statistical significance and validation comprehensiveness.
OpenEval R15 evaluates oncogenic function summary (C103-C105) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates related xenograft claims (C104) as SUPPORTED without specific critique.
OpenEval R15 includes cell cycle effects (C103-C105) as SUPPORTED. Peer R9 evaluates cell cycle data (C103) as SUPPORTED as part of convincing experimental work.
OpenEval R2 includes C27 (no effect on c-Myc) as part of specificity controls, finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R12 also finds this negative control (C27, C130) SUPPORTED without challenge.
OpenEval R11 synthesizes the overall mechanism (C121-C123) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C121 in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation of the mechanistic model.
OpenEval R16 evaluates the CNBP guiding mechanism summary (C111) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C111 in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation of the core mechanism.
OpenEval R10 addresses cis vs trans regulation (C114-C120). Peer R1 includes C117 in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation, with peer R11 explicitly supporting trans regulation.
OpenEval R12 evaluates poor sequence conservation of LAST (C124) as SUPPORTED and appropriately acknowledged. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this limitation.

OpenEval R13 evaluates established knowledge from literature (C2, C7-C10, C40-C41, C65, C91-C102, C109-C110, C112-C113, C125-C134) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel claims rather than background literature.
